other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) Reviews at [150], [164] and [177] asked to confirm the new lead matter's practice group and execution; the agent added a scope caveat calling it an M&A matter with an employment workstream and kept it.

divergence: All three runs fail by naming another matter as the latest. Two different routes led there. T0 and T2 never opened the settlement matter, although it surfaced in their store-wide scans. T0 then picked candidates by matter number and practice-area guesses; T2 picked six other matters from an engagement-letter classification table that listed it (surfaced-not-opened). Both then wrote draft or M&A employment agreements as the precedent. T1 read the matter's executed settlement agreement, but wrote a later litigation matter as the latest, on the strength of an affidavit describing a separation agreement it never opened, and kept the settlement only as a fallback. The reviews flagged hand-picked candidate sets in generic terms. In T1 and T2 they also named the weak basis of the final pick (an affidavit only; unclear practice group). The agents re-read or reworded but kept the matter. The agent-defined stages (batched scan, candidate verification, practice-group classification, recency cross-check, final consistency checks) did not change the outcome.
